name: Mississippi
agency: Mississippi Department of Public Safety, Driver Service Bureau
permitAge: 15 (regular learner's permit); 14 if enrolled in a certified driver education program, valid only for the driver education car

teen.holdPermit: Conflicting: Mississippi Administrative Code rule 31-1-2-18 says 6 months for 15-16 year olds; several secondary sources say 12 months. Not used in questions.
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate license: may drive alone 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.; other hours need a licensed driver 21+ (admin. code; one practice site gives 11:30 p.m. on Fri/Sat, unconfirmed)
teen.phone: All drivers: no texting, email or social media while driving since July 1, 2015 (HB 389); hands-free and voice-operated use allowed. 2009 law (SB 2280) banned texting for permit and intermediate holders. Under-18 wireless ban claimed by one secondary source only.

notes: Learner's permit holder drives with licensed adult 21+ in the front seat.
Intermediate license at 16. Unrestricted at 16.5 or 17 depending on source (conflict).
Exam: 30 questions, 24 correct (80%), computer-based, per third-party sites only (not confirmed on an official page).
Speed (Miss. Code 63-3-501): 65 mph general state highway max; Transportation Commission may raise interstates and 4+ lane controlled-access highways to 70 mph max; 2025 bill for 75 mph died.

Move over (Miss. Code 63-3-809): emergency, tow, MDOT, utility, sanitation vehicles with flashing lights; change lanes if safe, otherwise slow down and be prepared to stop. Fine $250, up to $1,000 with damage or injury.

School bus (Nathan's Law, 2011): stop at least 10 feet away; opposite direction need not stop on divided highway with at least two lanes each way; same direction must stop. First offense $350-$750; repeat can be a felony.
Right on red after full stop unless signed (Miss. Code 63-3-309); left on red only one-way to one-way.
Official DPS pages and handbook could not be found or fetched from this environment. A Spanish manual is claimed only by third-party driving-tests.org.
